newsitem.title: USA: U.S. suit covers about 300 Lloyd's investors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. suit covers about 300 Lloyd's investors.

text.p: A U.S. lawsuit against Lloyd's of London involves only about 300 investors, whose losses range in magnitude from $500,000 to $1 million, an attorney familiar with the case said.
A federal appeals court decision on Thursday cleared the way for Lloyd's investors, known as Names, to sue Lloyd's under securities fraud and racketeering legislation.
However, most of the U.S. Names last year accepted an offer from Lloyd's to settle litigation.

It is unclear whether or not the Names who accepted the settlement and the several hundred Names who did not settle and did not participate in this lawsuit will be able to benefit from the court's decision, said Ken Chiate, who has represented a number of Names in their litigation against Lloyd's.
American Names Association president Richard Rosenblatt doubted that damages payable to Names would reach $1 billion.
"I think we're dealing with in the United States, possibly 300 people," Rosenblatt said. "I don't think $1 billion is realistic."
Lloyd's expects to appeal the decision, which it described as erroneous.
Lloyd's has 14 days in which to file its appeal, spokesman William Pitt said.
